heading: Direct vs Regular Mutual Funds: Understanding SEBI's New Default Rule
tldr: Regular mutual funds include a commission for distributors, leading to higher expense ratios.
Direct mutual funds do not include distributor commissions, resulting in lower expense ratios.
SEBI's new rule mandates that execution-only platforms must offer direct plans as the default option for investors who do not seek advice.
This regulatory change aims to empower investors by potentially increasing their long-term wealth through lower costs.
Investors should review their existing mutual fund holdings and consider switching to direct plans where appropriate to maximise returns.
caption:
Ever wondered if you're paying too much for your mutual funds? There are two types: one includes fees for advice, and the other doesn't. A new rule now makes the lower-fee option the default on some platforms if you're managing your own investments. This could mean more money in your pocket over time! Learn how this change can benefit you. Read the full article to understand more.
